message:
docs(release): the deployment already chose, and one size was copied not read

The operations section offered two ways to terminate TLS and then described
one of them as if it were the arrangement. This server picked the other:
nginx forwards to an HTTPS upstream on loopback and the directory server
holds the certificate. Both the plan and the handoff now say so, and say not
to overwrite it. The loopback proxy_ssl_verify off is recorded as existing
configuration -- nothing here adds or widens a verification bypass, and the
product's own certificate checking is untouched.

Corrected with it: the 0.2.16 APK size. I wrote 11,518,126 for both APKs
because I carried the number from the earlier build instead of reading the
file, and the rebuilt one is 11,846,438. The manifest was generated from the
files and had the right value throughout, so nothing downstream was wrong --
but a size in prose that nobody re-read is exactly the kind of number that
gets trusted later.

Checking that led somewhere useful. "The two builds differ only in version"
is now verified rather than asserted: comparing the archives entry by entry,
two entries differ -- AndroidManifest.xml and classes3.dex, both carrying
version constants -- and the other 118 match down to their CRCs. The file
sizes differ anyway, from archive packing rather than content, so the
handoff warns against expecting them to match.

Added for the NAS: the confirmed configuration, the static artifact path as
a decision with its conditions and total size, the immutable per-version
path rule, an atomic manifest swap, the code contract (two detached files in,
one envelope out; platform whitelist; what the publish-time check does and
does not do when the key env is absent), and two things the NAS must confirm
rather than assume -- that the running process actually has the key, and
that the same 128 characters appear in all three places.
